messages:
maria: Heads-up — p99 for /v1/generate on the dashboard shows ~250ms better for EU Dedicated vs Hosted, but support has a customer citing worse tail. Can someone sanity-check sample origin + routing weights?
jon: Hmm. Which dashboard view are you looking at? route-level or deployment-level?
maria: route-level, endpoint filter set to /v1/generate, time range last 30m, aggregation = p99. I grabbed the query from Console -> Inspect Query.
sean: Can you paste the exact inspect query? UI sometimes hides that we aggregate across fallback routes.
maria: Here —
```sql
SELECT percentile(lat_ms, 99) AS p99, count(*)
FROM requests
WHERE route='/v1/generate' AND timestamp >= now() - interval '30 minutes'
GROUP BY deployment, region
```
jon: That looks fine. Two common causes: (1) different sample_source between deployments (console might show merged sample that mixes proxy-sampled and server-sampled streams) (2) routing fallback weights: hosted might be routing some traffic to cheaper replicas with higher tail.
ashok: @maria can you confirm whether the hosted rows include requests that were *retried* by client? Retries can hide true request latency if only the first attempt is logged differently.
maria: Good call. I checked logs — hosted shows ~3% higher retry_count for that route in EU.
jean (typo)
jon: (lol) jean -> sean?
sean: I can look at tracing; if client retries are counted on the service side differently we might be computing p99 over attempt-level latency instead of end-to-end attempt chain.
eva: Quick data check: when we compute p99 in the telemetry pipeline we have sample_source tag: {"proxy_sampled", "server_full"}. Console currently defaults to mixing both and doesn't surface the tag in the legend.
ashok: That's the UX issue. Users assume p99 is "user-observed" but we mix samples with different semantics. We should surface sample_source and route_weight in the legend.
maria: Agreed. Also the routing policy changed yesterday to add a fallback variant with lower memory (quantized). That variant has higher p95/p99 but lower cost — possibly where hosted was shifting.\evaluator-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for rollout/variant-quant-20260320 at 1711213200
jon: Thanks @deploy-bot. To debug: can we compute p99 by sample_source and by variant? Simple split might show which bucket drives the skew.
eva: Ran a quick split — p99 by sample_source for hosted (last 30m): proxy_sampled=480ms, server_full=720ms. For dedicated: proxy_sampled=420ms, server_full=450ms. So hosted server_full higher.
sean: That suggests hosted is seeing a heavier tail on the server-full stream. Could be model-variant fallback or region congestion. Let's check route->backend mapping.
maria: In routing table, hosted eu-west traffic has a 0.15 fallback weight to quantized-variant. Dedicated had 0.05.
ashok: So weighting differs. Dashboard currently shows an aggregated p99 that doesn't expose "weighting by route" vs "weighting by raw counts". That can confuse people: p99 is count-weighted, but fallbacks inflate the tail if they have higher latency even at small weight.\jon: UX proposal: add an aggregation dropdown with options: "count-weighted pctl", "route-weighted pctl", and "sample-source filter". Also show top contributing route variants with sparkline.
sean: Implementation note: frontend needs the top-3 contributors API from telemetry, and a small supplier of (route, weight, p95,p99). We already have an endpoint but it's expensive to compute at high cadence. Perhaps cache at 1m.
maria: Ops concern: computing variant-level p99 across all routes for every dashboard tile could spike costs. Let's start by surfacing the sample_source and variant tag for the selected route/time, then lazy-load contributor breakdown on demand.
jon: Agreed. Short-term mitigation: annotate the p99 tooltip with "sample_sources: server_full=3k, proxy_sampled=50k" and a note if retries > 1%. That will explain differences to users.
\eprints
sean: For the backend query change we should ensure we use the same percentile algorithm as the dashboard (tdigest vs histogram). We had a mismatch last quarter that caused small diffs.
maria: Good call. Which algo do we standardize on? tdigest in offline and approx-quantiles in streaming. Need to document.
eva: I'll add a small doc in telemetry repo: "percentile_contract.md" with exact method and sample_source semantics.
ashok: Action items: (1) frontend: surface sample_source and variant tag in legend + tooltip (sean) (2) backend: add contributor breakdown API (eva) (3) ops: add tooltip showing retry_rate and sample counts (jon) (4) doc: percentile_contract.md (eva) (5) short-term UX: annotate p99 with counts and sample_sources (sean + maria)
maria: I'm happy to shepherd the UX tooltip copy. If we do the lazy-load contributor breakdown, we can avoid large backend QPS.
jon: I'll also add a temporary alert rule: if sample_source mix changes >10% in 5m for any route, fire a page to eng-platform so we can catch rollout-induced tail regressions.
sean: I'll prototype the tooltip tomorrow and post screenshots.
maria: Thanks all. If nobody objects I'll file a lightweight RFC and a dashboard ticket. cc @ashok for prioritization.\ashok: Fine by me. Prioritize the tooltip + counts first. Schedule the contributor API in the next sprint.
maria: Cool — I'll open the ticket and tag the owners. Closing here for now :thumbsup:
